perspective: A published contract version is judged from the point of view of an existing, correctly-written CLIENT of the API — the side that does not control the change. major: any change that can make a correct existing client fail (request narrowing, response changes a client may not handle, security/credential invalidation). minor: backward-compatible additions and announced (with-sunset) deprecations. patch: no effect on the wire contract (docs/description/example/tag/operationId-only changes where the generated SDK surface is unchanged) — NOTE: unlike a pure wire-contract reading, operationId renames and tag changes DO move/rename generated SDK methods (openapi-python-client, @hey-api/openapi-ts), so both are judged major here, not patch. Any rule id absent from this map is major by Rob's fail-safe ruling.
